ingredientSections.heading: Pizza Margherita
items: 3 Cups tomato sauce (hand crushed San Marzano tomatoes and sea salt to taste)
2 x 250g balls mozzarella di bufala di campagna
100g Grana Padano or Parmigiano Reggiano, grated

methodSections.heading: Pizza Dough
steps: Start this process the day before pizza day to give the dough time to develop character, or at least early in the morning for that evening's dinner.
Dissolve the salt in the water in a large mixing bowl and mix in about 10 percent of the flour.
Measure the yeast and carefully mix it in.
Add and stir through the remaining flour and knead together until even.
Continue to knead on a lightly floured work surface until the dough is smooth and not too sticky.
Place the dough in a large container with lid and allow to ferment overnight. Keep in mind the dough will quadruple in size.
Divide the dough into 7 balls. The 7th ball can be used to make a flatbread for the burrata plate, previous page.
Place on 2-3 cookie sheets or trays and cover with plastic bags so they don't dry out but have room to grow.
Dough can be kept in the fridge for up to 3 days, but bring the dough balls back to room temperature for around an hour before using.

methodSections.heading: Pizza Margherita
steps: Preheat the oven to its highest setting with a pizza stone on the middle rack.
Using a floured surface, stretch dough into 12in bases.
Place a base on a lightly floured pizza peel or inverted round baking tray.
Spread 125ml tomato sauce. Starting in the middle and working outward and stopping 3-4cm before the edge.
Sprinkle the grated cheese around evenly.
Break up 1/3 of a ball of the mozzarella and arrange on the base.
Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.
Shimmy and slide the base onto the hot pizza stone and bake for 3-4 minutes or until golden and crispy. You can also try switching the oven to broil to give the pizza a blast of top heat.
Garnish with basil leaves and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Repeat with the remaining dough.
